```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 5,
  fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 144, out.width = "100%", dev = "ragg_png")
```

A geom draws a shape from mapped data. A stat computes new values or geometry before drawing. This article gives a small example of every three-dimensional geom and stat. Installation is covered in [Get started](ggplot3d.html).

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggplot3d)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 16) + theme(
  axis.text = element_text(size = 13), legend.position = "none"))
```

## Points, paths, segments and text

Each row below contains a position and a label. Points draw one mark per row. Paths connect rows in their input order within each group.

```{r points, fig.alt="Three blue points in three dimensions."}
d <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 2), y = c(0, 2, 1), z = c(1, 3, 2),
                label = c("a", "b", "c"))
p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y, z = z))
p + geom_point_3d(size = 3, colour = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

```{r paths, fig.alt="A blue path connecting the same three positions in input order."}
p + geom_path_3d(linewidth = 0.8, colour = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

Segments use a start and an endpoint from each row. Text places labels at the mapped positions. A dropline joins each position to the selected face of the data box.

```{r segments, fig.alt="Three blue segments dropping to z equal to zero."}
p + geom_segment_3d(aes(xend = x, yend = y, zend = 0),
                     linewidth = 0.8, colour = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

```{r text, fig.alt="The labels a, b and c at three positions."}
p + geom_text_3d(aes(label = label), size = 5) + coord_3d()
```

```{r droplines, fig.alt="Three points with lines connecting them to the floor of the box."}
p + geom_dropline_3d(face = "zmin", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 3) + coord_3d()
```

## Polygons and bands

A polygon is an ordered ring of vertices in a plane after position transformations; the triangle below lies on a sloping plane. Use a group for each feature and a subgroup for each ring when a feature has holes.

```{r polygon, fig.alt="A blue triangular polygon in a sloping plane."}
triangle <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1), z = c(0, 1, 1))
ggplot(triangle, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_polygon_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

A band joins two boundaries. Mapping zmin and zmax produces a vertical wall along the x/y path. Six endpoint aesthetics can describe a band with boundaries that also differ in x and y.

```{r band, fig.alt="A blue vertical band following a sine curve."}
band <- data.frame(x = seq(0, 4, length.out = 16), y = 0)
band$low <- sin(band$x)
band$high <- band$low + 0.5
ggplot(band, aes(x, y, zmin = low, zmax = high)) +
  geom_band_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

## Surfaces and contours

A gridded surface connects adjacent pairs of x/y coordinates with triangles. Scattered points can use Delaunay triangulation, which connects nearby points in the transformed x/y plane, with `method = "delaunay"`. Within each group, each x/y pair must be unique.

```{r surface, fig.alt="A curved blue surface sampled on a regular grid."}
surface <- expand.grid(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 10),
                       y = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 10))
surface$z <- with(surface, exp(-(x^2 + y^2) / 2))
s <- ggplot(surface, aes(x, y, z = z))
s + geom_surface_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

The surface stat exposes the triangulation step. The computed height `z_mean` is the mean height of each triangle and can be mapped to fill after the stat has run.

```{r stat-surface, fig.alt="A curved surface coloured by each triangle's mean height."}
s + stat_surface_3d(aes(fill = after_stat(z_mean))) + coord_3d()
```

Contours trace equal heights. Filled contours draw bands between height thresholds. The plane argument chooses the surface, the floor, or a fixed height in original units.

```{r contours, fig.alt="Height contours on a curved surface."}
s + geom_contour_3d(bins = 4, linewidth = 0.8) + coord_3d()
```

```{r filled-contours, fig.alt="Filled height bands projected onto the floor of the data box."}
s + geom_contour_filled_3d(bins = 4, plane = "floor") + coord_3d()
```

## Columns, counts and extrusions

Columns occupy cells on an x/y lattice and extend from a baseline to z. A bar layer counts observations at each x/y combination. The count stat gives direct access to that calculation.

```{r columns, fig.alt="Nine blue columns with heights from one to nine."}
columns <- expand.grid(x = 1:3, y = 1:3)
columns$z <- seq_len(nrow(columns))
ggplot(columns, aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_col_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

```{r bars, fig.alt="Columns showing counts of cars by cylinder and gear categories."}
counts <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), factor(gear)))
counts + geom_bar_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-count, fig.alt="The count stat drawing counts of cars by cylinder and gear categories."}
counts + stat_count_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

Extrusion extends an ordered x/y polygon between two heights. The z value gives its endpoint. The `base` argument supplies the starting height; a mapped zmin overrides it. Caps close the top and bottom.

```{r extrusion, fig.alt="A blue rectangular polygon extruded to a height of two."}
ring <- data.frame(x = c(0, 2, 2, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1), z = 2)
ggplot(ring, aes(x, y, z = z)) + geom_extrude_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") +
  coord_3d()
```

Stacking accumulates column heights separately above and below zero. It requires a linear continuous z scale and a shared zero baseline. Nudging shifts positions in transformed units.

```{r positions, fig.alt="Two coloured column sections stacked at a single x/y position."}
stack <- data.frame(x = 1, y = 1, z = c(2, 3), part = c("a", "b"))
ggplot(stack, aes(x, y, z = z, fill = part)) +
  geom_col_3d(position = position_stack_3d()) + coord_3d()
```

## Indexed meshes

A mesh describes vertices and faces using integer indices. Indices start at one. Each row in the face matrix identifies the corners of a triangle or quadrilateral. The mesh constructor returns a corner table keyed by vertex, face and corner.

```{r mesh, fig.alt="A sloping quadrilateral supplied as an indexed mesh."}
vertices <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 1, 0), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
                       z = c(0, 0, 1, 1))
mesh <- mesh_3d(vertices, matrix(1:4, nrow = 1))
ggplot() + geom_mesh_3d(data = mesh, fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

## Function and fitted surfaces

Function surfaces sample a vectorized function of x and y. The grid is evenly spaced in transformed x and y coordinates. Function inputs and returned z values use original data units. The z scale transforms the returned heights.

```{r function, fig.alt="A sampled sine-cosine surface."}
ggplot() + geom_function_3d(fun = function(x, y) sin(x) * cos(y), n = 10) +
  xlim(-2, 2) + ylim(-2, 2) + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-function, fig.alt="The function stat sampling a quadratic surface."}
ggplot() + stat_function_3d(fun = function(x, y) x^2 + y^2, n = 10) +
  xlim(-1, 1) + ylim(-1, 1) + coord_3d()
```

Fitted surfaces model z using x and y. Fitting and prediction use transformed positions. The linear model's default formula is z as a function of x plus y. Confidence surfaces, when requested, describe pointwise uncertainty in the conditional mean.

```{r smooth, fig.alt="A fitted linear surface for a grid with a deterministic curved deviation."}
fit_data <- surface
fit_data$z <- with(fit_data, x + y + sin(3 * x * y) / 5)
f <- ggplot(fit_data, aes(x, y, z = z))
f + geom_smooth_3d(method = "lm", se = FALSE, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-smooth, fig.alt="The smooth stat drawing a fitted linear response surface."}
f + stat_smooth_3d(method = "lm", se = FALSE, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

## Density surfaces and ridges

A bivariate density surface estimates how observations are distributed over x and y. Its height is density, computed with a Gaussian product kernel. The bandwidth controls smoothing along each input axis.

```{r density2d, fig.alt="A density surface for eruption duration and waiting time in the faithful data."}
ggplot(faithful, aes(eruptions, waiting)) +
  stat_density_2d_3d(n = 12) + coord_3d()
```

Ridgelines estimate a one-dimensional density for each group and place the groups along the perpendicular axis. Here each species occupies a single y position. Height multiplies the density in transformed z units.

```{r ridge, fig.alt="Three density ridges for sepal length, one per iris species."}
r <- ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Length, as.numeric(Species),
                     group = Species, fill = Species))
r + geom_ridgeline_3d(n = 24) + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-ridge, fig.alt="The ridgeline stat drawing the same species-specific sepal length densities."}
r + stat_ridgeline_3d(n = 24) + coord_3d()
```

## Scalar-field level surfaces

A scalar field assigns a numeric value to each x/y/z position. An isosurface joins positions with the same field value. Supply a complete rectilinear grid and map the field to `value`; missing field values mask their incident cells.

```{r isosurface, fig.alt="A level surface of squared distance from the origin."}
field <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8),
  y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8), z = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 8))
field$value <- with(field, x^2 + y^2 + z^2)
v <- ggplot(field, aes(x, y, z = z, value = value))
v + geom_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6, fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-isosurface, fig.alt="The isosurface stat extracting the same squared-distance threshold."}
v + stat_isosurface_3d(levels = 0.6, fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

A function can supply field values directly. It receives transformed coordinates in all three axes. Grid resolution sets how finely the function is sampled.

```{r isofunction, fig.alt="A spherical level surface sampled from a three-variable function."}
ball <- function(x, y, z) x^2 + y^2 + z^2
ggplot() + geom_isofunction_3d(fun = ball, n = 8, levels = 0.5) +
  xlim(-1, 1) + ylim(-1, 1) + zlim(-1, 1) + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-isofunction, fig.alt="The isofunction stat sampling the squared-distance function."}
ggplot() + stat_isofunction_3d(fun = ball, n = 8, levels = 0.5) +
  xlim(-1, 1) + ylim(-1, 1) + zlim(-1, 1) + coord_3d()
```

## Trivariate density

A trivariate density estimates the distribution of observations in three dimensions. Numeric levels select density thresholds. Probability contents, specified with `probs()`, select enclosed mass estimated from the sampled grid. The grid ranges need to include the density tails for probability-content requests.

```{r isodensity, fig.alt="A density level surface around a deterministic three-dimensional point sample."}
set.seed(4)
cloud <- data.frame(x = rnorm(40), y = rnorm(40), z = rnorm(40))
c <- ggplot(cloud, aes(x, y, z = z))
c + geom_isodensity_3d(h = 0.7, levels = 0.02, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-density, fig.alt="The density stat extracting a level surface from the same sample."}
c + stat_density_3d(h = 0.7, levels = 0.02, n = 8) + coord_3d()
```

```{r}
probs(0.5, 0.9)
```

## Convex hulls

A convex hull is the smallest convex shape containing the input positions. This example uses the eight corners of a cube. Coplanar input produces a planar polygon, and collinear input produces no faces.

```{r hull, fig.alt="The convex hull of the eight corners of a cube."}
corners <- expand.grid(x = 0:1, y = 0:1, z = 0:1)
h <- ggplot(corners, aes(x, y, z = z))
h + geom_hull_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

```{r stat-hull, fig.alt="The hull stat drawing the cube defined by the same eight corners."}
h + stat_hull_3d(fill = "#2E6F9E") + coord_3d()
```

## Adapting a layer

The layer adapter equips a registered ggplot2 geom with three-dimensional scene emission. Extension authors register an emitter to describe how another geom produces geometry. The registration help page describes the callback arguments.

```{r adapter, fig.alt="Three points drawn by an adapted ggplot2 point layer."}
p + layer_3d(geom_point(size = 3)) + coord_3d()
```
